title: Pin-event signal router: tenant-aware eval ignition and smoke policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, tenant-aware routing layer that listens for model version pin/upgrades (catalog or customer-pinned) and triggers targeted evals with adaptive sampling and budget controls. The router should enrich pin events with tenant metadata, compute a sampling decision, and emit eval requests to the existing eval-runner API without overloading downstream systems or incurring unbounded cost.

Background: Current pin-triggered eval flows are primarily PM-driven and monolithic: catalog changes fan out broad eval jobs which are expensive; customer pins lack consistent smoke checks. We need a unified signal layer that reduces noise, respects tenant budgets, and supports quick, low-cost smoke checks plus priority-driven full-fidelity evals when necessary.

Scope:
- Subscribe to pin-change events (catalog and tenant scopes).
- Enrich events with tenant profile (usage tier, historical regression risk, opt-outs, budget allowance).
- Decide eval firing mode: 1) quick smoke (low-cost synthetic probes), 2) sampled fidelity eval (subset of synths weighted by drift/risk), 3) prioritized full eval (high-risk tenants or critical catalog promotions).
- Implement cost guard: per-tenant and global rate limits, daily budget caps, and backpressure to eval-runner.
- Emit standardized eval request payloads and tags to support observability and traceability.
- Provide a management endpoint to preview event decisions and override sampling for emergency rollbacks.

Design notes:
- Event dedupe window: 10m for identical pin events to avoid duplicate evals during churn.
- Sampling policy: base probability = f(tenant_usage_score, recent_regressions, model_sensitivity). Weighted uplift for enterprise tiers.
- Tenant budget enforcement: consult tenant_budget_service; if budget exhausted, fall back to minimal smoke or create a queued ticket for manual review.
- Failure modes: if eval-runner returns 5xx or is throttled, mark event as RETRY with exponential backoff up to 6 hours; if persistent, notify PM owner and create incident task.
- Telemetry: emit decision_reason, sample_rate, budget_status, downstream_latency, and eval_result_id when available.

APIs & hooks:
- Ingest: /internal/pins/stream (event-driven) or pubsub subscription.
- Management: /internal/pins/preview?tenant=...&model=... returns predicted decision and cost estimate.
- Emit: POST /internal/evals/requests with tags [pin_source, tenant_id, sample_type, decision_id].

Testing plan: unit tests for sampling heuristics, integration test against a sandbox eval-runner with simulated throttles, canary rollout in staging and a small set of low-risk tenants, and post-rollout audit of cost vs. expectations for 48h.

Artifacts: Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVAL/Pin+Signal+Router (draft). Spike PR with prototype logic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-scripts/pull/214 (prototype).
acceptance_criteria: Router subscribes to pin-change events and enriches with tenant metadata within 1s median time
Sampling decision logic is unit-tested and deterministic for fixed seed
Router can emit smoke eval requests and full eval requests to eval-runner with appropriate tags
Per-tenant budget checks prevent eval dispatch when budget flag exhausted and fall back to predetermined minimal smoke
System enforces global rate limits and exposes a backpressure signal that eval-runner honors
Management preview endpoint returns consistent decision and cost estimate and is covered by integration tests
Telemetry emitted for 100% of decisions: decision_id, reason, sample_rate, budget_status, downstream_result_id (if available)
comments: 2026-01-20 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff sync completed. Agreed to use existing tenant_budget_service for enforcement and reuse eval-runner API. Follow-up: Marco to propose proto for decision payload.
2026-02-02 - Marco Ruiz: Prototype for sampling function uploaded in spike branch. Early numbers look promising; synthetic smoke reduces token usage by ~80% on catalog pin tests.
2026-02-18 - PM review (Lina Gomez): PM requests explicit tenant opt-out handling and a flag for enterprise override. Added to ACs.
2026-02-28 - Security review note (Rajiv Menon): No customer data returned by router; ensures KMS keys not used. Security review not required but audit log must be retained 90 days.

2026-03-05 - Marco Ruiz: Integration tests added. Discovered race when two pin events arrive simultaneously for same tenant; implemented 10m dedupe and fixed bug in dedupe key computation. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routers/pull/57

2026-03-09 - QA (Nora Chen): Canary in staging passed for 24h across 10 tenants. Observed 1.2% higher-than-expected smoke-trigger rate due to tuning error; adjusted baseline probabilities. Next step: small prod canary for non-enterprise tenants.
2026-03-10 - Marco Ruiz: Ready for production canary rollout tickets. Created rollout plan in Confluence and assigned ops on-call for first 48h monitoring.
